---
title: "Lab 04 — Probability through simulation"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
voters <- read_csv("data/FLVoters.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(race), !is.na(gender))
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab04", title = "Probability through simulation", open = "q4")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "A probability of 0.30 for an event means…",
  q2 = "If you repeat a small sample many times, the estimated share…",
  q3 = "P(Black | woman) in this voter file is…",
  q4 = "Why is “conflict is likely” not yet a probability statement?"
)
```

## What you will do

Treat probability as a long-run share, then read a conditional share in the Florida voter file. Download the `.txt`.

```{r sim, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=5}
set.seed(4)
mean(rbinom(20, size = 1, prob = 0.30))
mean(rbinom(5000, size = 1, prob = 0.30))
```

```{r cond, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=4}
mean(voters$race == "black")
mean(voters$race[voters$gender == "f"] == "black")
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("In a long run of identical trials, the event occurs about 30 percent of the time.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("This particular trial is 30 percent true."),
  answer("The event is rare, so we can ignore it."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Jumps around. A long run sits near the probability.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Equals 0.30 in every sample of 20."),
  answer("Becomes a causal effect once the sample is large."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("The share of women who are recorded as Black (about 0.14), not the share of all voters who are Black.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The same number as the share of voters who are Black women."),
  answer("Proof that gender causes race."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "A probability names an event and a reference set.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
